confirmed_fact: Council street lights are maintained under a PFI contract with Tay Valley Lighting, with services by Enerveo. Faults on lights with the Enerveo label are reported online via the Enerveo portal or on 0800 048 2436. Lights without the label may be privately owned: contact the owner shown on the column.
Since 1 December 2023 street lighting is switched off between 1am and 5.30am, in certain areas of the city.
Drains and gullies, railings, road signs, traffic lights and crossings, faded markings, grit bins and paving are reported on the council's 'report a road or street problem' form.
The council only considers road safety improvements if injury accident data shows incidents involving personal injury within the last three years.
Vandalism or damage to a bus shelter can be reported to the council on its bus stop or shelter form.
source_name: Report a problem with a bus stop or shelter

confirmed_fact: The council cannot fine vehicles parked dangerously or causing an obstruction where there is no parking restriction. These can only be dealt with by the police: call Hampshire Constabulary on 101.
source_name: Incorrectly parked cars or parking offences

confirmed_fact: A faulty pay and display machine can be reported on the council's online form, which also takes refund claims. Refunds are investigated, not automatic.

Replacing a green-lidded general waste bin costs £35 for 140 litre and £45 for 240 litre. Charges are non-refundable. The council no longer provides 360 litre general waste bins: call 023 8083 3005. Other bins are replaced free.
source_name: My bin is lost or stolen
caveat: Replaces the existing charges row (£33/£43/£54), which no longer matches the page.

confirmed_fact: Any type of damaged bin is replaced free of charge. Replacement bins can take up to eight weeks to be delivered.
Residents should put bins out before 6.30am on collection day and take them back by 11.59pm. The council asks residents to speak to the neighbour first, then use its form.
If you believe that you or someone else may be in danger, call the police on 999.
Problems with drains or overflowing manholes outside a property's boundary usually lie with Southern Water (033 0303 0368), with exceptions. Tenants should tell their landlord.
One sighting of a rat outside a property generally needs no report. Rats in a public space can be reported to the council on its nuisance form.

A council-owned tree that is dangerous is treated as an emergency. A tree that is an immediate hazard to life or property is reported on the 'tree in a dangerous condition' form. For a private tree, contact the landowner first.
source_name: Reporting issues with trees or vegetation

confirmed_fact: The council does not carry out tree work for television reception, obstructed light or views, seasonal debris, overhang into gardens or parking areas, or general size.
To report an emergency with an overhead power line, call SSE on 0800 0727 282.

Council tenants report emergency repairs by phone, not online: 023 8083 3006 (option two) in office hours, 023 8023 3344 outside them. Emergency means immediate danger to you, your family or property.
Emergency repairs are usually done the same day, within four hours; urgent repairs within two days; prioritised standard repairs get an appointment within 10 days; standard repairs within 25 days.

Call 999 if there is a danger to life. Southern Water has a 24-hour emergency line on 0330 303 0368. Non-life threatening flooding can be reported to the council on its form or on 023 8083 3000 in office hours.
